transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Feldman (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood CSM), Priya Menon (AceroHealth ML Eng), Carlos Ortega (AceroHealth Platform), Dana Liu (AceroHealth CTO), Tom Nguyen (AceroHealth SRE)

---
Summary note: quick sync on throughput and queueing; focus on continuous batching and concurrency targets. Marcus will run the larger concurrency test and Carlos will enable debug logs for KV cache.

00:00 Lena Park: all right hey everyone good to see you, um this is the weekly pilot sync for Acero, thanks for making the time. Quick roll call?
00:08 Priya Menon: hey hi here, Priya on ML, Carlos is joining, Tom is on as well.
00:13 Carlos Ortega: yep here, thanks.
00:15 Lena Park: perfect. Marcus do you wanna kick off with the results from the last run?
00:20 Marcus Feldman: yeah, sure. So we ran the continuous-batching-v1 profile from last week, and the headline - p50 improved from 110ms to about 92ms under the 4x concurrency baseline, but p95 didn't move much, it was around 760 to 740ms. We dug in and saw the queue depth has spiky tail behavior when many short requests arrive together which defeats some of the batching heuristics.
00:46 Priya Menon: and on our side we saw some KV cache misses, like 12% of requests had cold prefix misses which bumped the tail a lot. Could be because session affinity wasn't sticky in staging.
01:00 Marcus Feldman: yeah I think that's the combination - admission control allowed bursts in that caused variable batch sizes and then cold cache add-on latency. We also saw token counts vary a lot; the model decode length jittered which changed kernel selection.
01:18 Dana Liu: quick question, is the p95 we measured inclusive of network hop time? I want to make sure we're comparing apples to apples vs our internal microservice latencies.
01:26 Tom Nguyen: we used synthetic client on the same VPC so network is minimal, most of that was server-side.
01:31 Lena Park: good callout. Marcus, what's your hypothesis for the queueing fix?
01:36 Marcus Feldman: couple things. One, tighten admission control so we cap queue depth per worker to limit worst-case batch formation, two, increase concurrency from 4x to 8x for a short canary to reduce batch waiting time, and three, pre-warm the KV cache by replaying prefixes from the warmup script - that should reduce cold misses. Also set a short batching timeout for small requests so they don't sit waiting for a full batch.
02:04 Priya Menon: when you say 8x concurrency, do you expect cost to spike linearly? We have a cost target and need to know tradeoffs.
02:13 Marcus Feldman: good question. Not linear necessarily — batching efficiency can improve per-token cost even as concurrency increases. For some workloads we saw cost per 1k tokens drop 6-12% when we raised concurrency due to larger avg batch sizes, but that's workload dependent. We'll surface per-token delta in the experiment.
02:30 Carlos Ortega: we also worry about hot shards and GPU memory warmup; if we double concurrency could that thrash the KV cache?
02:38 Marcus Feldman: it can if you oversubscribe kernels; but our runtime maintains per-shard KV caches and the prewarm script plus slightly larger cache allocation during the test should prevent thrashing. We'll monitor eviction rates.
02:51 Lena Park: ok sounds like a plan. Carlos, can you provision the dedicated staging pool we discussed? We want to avoid noisy neighbor stuff during the 8x run.
02:58 Carlos Ortega: yes I can. I'll allocate a 2-node dedicated pool in staging with the same model variant and enable full KV logs. That'll be ready by Sunday.
03:06 Aisha Khan: note — I've already shared the tuning playbook in the pilot folder, link's in the notes. It includes recommended admission settings and the prewarm script.
03:15 Priya Menon: great. Regarding quality — Priya here — we need to run the golden prompt set to sniff for regressions when batching changes. Marcus, will the test pipeline attach the golden set?
03:24 Marcus Feldman: yes, we'll run the golden set inline as part of the experiment so we can check sample outputs and a small automated regression metric. We'll push diffs to the spreadsheet.
03:33 Dana Liu: if the regression metrics move, what's rollback plan? We can't have degraded output in prod.
03:38 Marcus Feldman: rollback is immediate — we can revert concurrency and batching profile and fallback to the lower-cost model variant that has identical semantics. We also have automatic A/B split so 10% traffic can be routed to the canary first.
03:49 Tom Nguyen: also want to confirm logging and trace ids — we'll want full traces for slow tails.
03:54 Marcus Feldman: yes we'll include trace hook instrumentation; you should see per-request token timing and cache hit flags.
04:02 Priya Menon: quick transcribe hiccup, sometimes the 'KV' got transcribed as 'kay-v' in our logs — just a heads up for the auto tools.
04:09 Lena Park: ha yes Fireflies does that sometimes, we ignore it.
04:13 Marcus Feldman: moving on, technical detail: admission control change is basically a token-bucket with a hard queue length cap per worker, setBatchTimeout reduces to 8ms for small requests, and continuous-batching-v2 will prefer slightly larger max batch size but tighter timeout. That combination reduces wait jitter.
04:37 Priya Menon: 8ms seems aggressive — will that harm batching efficiency?
04:40 Marcus Feldman: for very short requests maybe but combined with higher concurrency it reduces overall latency while preserving token efficiency. We'll measure comparative cost.
04:51 Carlos Ortega: can you also log per-batch composition? I want to see how many short vs long requests are grouped.
04:55 Marcus Feldman: yep per-batch histograms will be turned on in staging.
05:00 Lena Park: ok let's go through the schedule for the 8x run — Marcus what do you need from the Acero side?
05:06 Marcus Feldman: need the staging pool provisioned, KV logs turned on, golden prompt set committed to the test repo, and a short window of low production traffic to reduce interference — maybe run at 02:00 UTC if that's feasible.
05:17 Carlos Ortega: we can do 02:00 UTC, staging window is clear.
05:20 Priya Menon: I can get the golden prompt set in by tomorrow morning.
05:24 Lena Park: great. Any blockers on the data residency or security side for enabling debug logs?
05:29 Dana Liu: logs are fine for staging, but make sure PII is redacted. We don't want raw patient identifiers in logs.
05:34 Marcus Feldman: yep we have a redaction pre-hook; traces will have hashed IDs only.
05:39 Aisha Khan: side note — on Dedicated burst pricing, there's a small premium for guaranteed capacity during the run window. Lena will follow up with numbers.
05:47 Lena Park: I'll send the delta this afternoon.
05:50 Tom Nguyen: from an SRE perspective, we want an alert if eviction rate > 3% or p95 jumps > 20% during the canary. Can you set that?
05:58 Marcus Feldman: yes we'll add those alerts and hook them into your PagerDuty.
06:03 Priya Menon: about the KV cache misses — we saw a pattern where new user sessions had higher misses; would session affinity or sticky keys help?
06:12 Marcus Feldman: session affinity helps; we can suggest a light sticky hashing by user id but beware that it reduces batching opportunity across users. For Acero's traffic pattern, a mild affinity (10s sticky) probably gives best tradeoff. We'll test both sticky and non-sticky in the experiment.
06:28 Carlos Ortega: can that sticky setting be rolled out via config flag? We need to avoid code changes.
06:31 Marcus Feldman: yes it's a runtime config; no code touch required.
06:35 Dana Liu: timeline wise, if the 8x run on Monday passes, how quickly could you move to a small Dedicated pilot in prod?
06:42 Lena Park: depends on contract sign-off, but from engineering side we can enable Dedicated burst within 48 hours of sign-off. We'll need legal to finish the amendment.
06:51 Dana Liu: ok we'll prioritize procurement.
06:54 Marcus Feldman: last technical note — we'll capture per-token cost delta, avg batch size, tail percentiles, KV hit rate, and eviction counts. I'll annotate the spreadsheet with these metrics and a short runbook for reproducing.
07:08 Priya Menon: great. A couple of small clarifications: when you say 'eviction counts' does that include cross-shard evictions?
07:14 Marcus Feldman: yes, we instrument cross-shard and per-shard eviction metrics separately.
07:19 Tom Nguyen: also request we keep the model variant pinned during the test; changing weights confounds results.
07:23 Marcus Feldman: agreed — we'll pin model v1.3.2 for the canary.
07:27 Lena Park: ok wrap-up — recap of next steps and owners? Marcus will run 8x, Carlos provisions pool and enables logs, Priya provides golden prompts, Lena sends pricing. We'll aim to reconvene after experiment with results.
07:41 Priya Menon: sounds good thanks all.
07:44 Lena Park: thanks everyone, I'll post notes and the benchmark link in the calendar invite.
07:49 Dana Liu: thanks.
07:51 Aisha Khan: thanks, bye.
07:53 Meeting end.
